updates.title: Everyone Sells the Same AI enters final interior review
updates.body: The full 6x9 interior is now laid out, with all ten figures in place and the front and back matter matched to the rest of the list. A last round of proof checks is under way before print files are prepared.

updates.title: Title confirmed: Who Authorised This?
updates.body: The title and subtitle are now set: Who Authorised This? When Machines Can Decide, Act, and Spend. The question mark is part of the book’s structure. The preface asks the question, the middle of the book brings it to a head, and the epilogue answers it.

updates.title: Welcome to Writ & Ledger Books
updates.body:
Every institution runs on a quiet assumption: that someone, somewhere, authorized what just happened. A trade was approved. A budget was released. A decision was made by a person who could explain it.

That assumption is starting to break. Software no longer just advises. It decides, acts and, increasingly, spends. Most organizations have not yet asked who holds authority when that happens, or what good judgement looks like when the better answer comes from a machine.

Writ & Ledger Books exists to ask those questions properly. We publish books for leaders in capital markets, private equity and the institutions around them: people who have to make real decisions about AI, not just read about it.

The list is built as one connected argument. Each book owns a single central question, so the titles add to each other instead of repeating each other. One asks why AI creates less value than promised in investment firms. Another asks how to choose between AI tools that all look the same. Others follow what happens when capital allocation itself becomes automated, and where human agreements and machine actions fall out of step.

Manufactured Value is available now on Kindle and Papaerback and Hardcover editions. The other titles are moving through production, and this page is where we'll share the progress: title decisions, cover reveals, release dates and the occasional essay.

If you'd like to hear when each book is ready, join the newsletter below. If you're a journalist, reviewer or event organizer, the Contact page is the quickest way to reach us.

Thank you for being here at the start.

Uttaran Chakrabarti
